relationships.evidence_quote: Recovery from inactivation, assessed using a paired-pulse protocol, was markedly slowed at lower temperatures and accelerated at higher temperatures

relationships.evidence_quote: Consequently, cumulative calcium influx at 13 °C was significantly increased by 1.8-fold (992 ± 98 pC/pF, n = 15; p < 0.0001) compared to 22 °C (546 ± 58 pC/pF, n = 15)

relationships.subject: Cav3.2 V416R
relationships.evidence_quote: these findings demonstrate that the V416R substitution broadly slows Cav3.2 gating kinetics while producing comparatively modest effects on steady-state voltage dependence

key_findings: Cooling slows Cav3.2 activation, inactivation, deactivation and recovery kinetics and reduces peak current, but during 50-100 Hz trains it increases cumulative calcium influx (temperature-dependent functional inversion).
The slow-gating Cav3.2 V416R variant reproduces low-temperature kinetics and attenuates the inversion.
